afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 140455
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
955 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 06Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A pair of weather systems moving through the region today and 
  tomorrow will bring rain chances back to the region and cool 
  temperatures to near to below normal.

- Sunday and Monday will be warm and dry before another weather
  disturbance brings occasional rain chances and cooling 
  temperatures back to the Desert Southwest by Tuesday.

- Another weather system could move through the region at the end of 
  next week that will help keep temperatures below normal. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
A shortwave trough is currently centered over SE CA/NW Mexico and
is moving into SW AZ as of early this afternoon. Out ahead of the
shortwave trough is a broken line of showers and a few embedded 
thunderstorms, stretching from Wickenburg down to Tucson. These 
showers have formed along the front and there is some low level 
frontogenesis, as seen on the SPC mesoanalysis, helping the 
showers along. These showers will continue to move northeastwards 
as the trough progresses eastward through the evening. There was a
lot more lightning activity earlier today when the activity was 
in SW AZ where there was some more instability (around 500 J/kg). 
However, there is some CIN (-25 J/kg) over south-central AZ, 
including the Phoenix Metro, so most of the activity is now just 
shower activity as it has moved away from the instability. This 
activity should push northeast of the Phoenix Metro by early this 
evening and then will be confined to the higher terrain areas. 
PWATs are only around 0.8- 1.0", so minimal accumulations are 
expected with most locations seeing less than 0.10" with some 
isolated locations seeing up to 0.25". 

Tomorrow, a secondary shortwave will move through the region. 
This shortwave is currently situated over the central CA and will 
quickly progress eastward, moving through northern AZ tomorrow. 
This shortwave will be weaker and will be further north. As a 
result isolated to scattered rain chances will be confined to the 
higher terrain and foothills north and east of Phoenix. Best 
chances will be during the overnight hours tonight and morning 
hours tomorrow with dry conditions returning by tomorrow evening. 
PWATs will be around 0.6-0.8" and there will be little to no 
instability. Therefore, rainfall accumulations will be light and 
generally around 0.10" or less. 

Some wind gusts of 20-30 mph are expected through the evening and
overnight hours. Highest gusts will be associated with the rain 
showers moving through central AZ and across SE CA. Higher gusts 
of 30-40 mph are possible across portions of SE CA, particularly 
the usual windy spot of the SW corner of Imperial County. 
Additionally, as a result of these two shortwave troughs 
temperatures will be on a decline. Afternoon high temperatures 
will be in the upper 70s to low 80s across SE CA and SW AZ. An 
abundance of cloud cover, and the rain currently moving through 
central AZ, will keep high temperatures in the low to mid 70s 
across the south-central AZ lower deserts. Matter of fact, areas 
across south-central AZ likely already reached their afternoon 
high temperature prior to the rain moving through. Across the 
higher terrain temperatures will be in the 60s. With the secondary
shortwave and additional cloud cover tomorrow, temperatures will 
cool even more. With highs in the mid to upper 70s across SE CA 
and SW AZ, in the low 70s across south- central AZ, and in the 50s
to mid 60s across the higher terrain areas. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
Sunday will be a down day for shower activity with a brief period
of shortwave ridging and some slight dry air advection from the 
northwest. This will lead to considerably less clouds, virtually 
no rain chances and temperatures climbing back into the upper 70s 
by Monday. Models remain in good agreement that another northern 
Pacific waves will continue to be ejected southeastward toward the
U.S. West Coast starting early next week. Currently models 
suggest the next potential system reaching the California coast 
early Monday before reaching our region Monday night into Tuesday,
where additional rain chances will return to the forecast with 
NBM PoPs peaking between 50-80% in south-central AZ and the higher
terrain areas, however this far out this may need to be adjusted 
based of how the track of this low progresses. By Wednesday models
are pointing towards yet again another low system, however larger
discrepancies between models are evident for this system. Due to 
this confidence is low for rain chances by mid to late next week 
as things are too inconsistent at this time. 

Despite if these next systems bring rain to the region or not, a 
more significant cooling trend can be counted on by the middle of 
the week as these series of weather systems move in from the 
northwest. They will likely usher in a cooler air mass with 
afternoon highs trending more towards the upper 60s to low 70s, 
the higher or lower end of this range largely being dependent on 
the depth and position of the systems. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0455Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
Extended periods of SCT to BKN clouds down to 3500-6000 ft AGL
will be the primary aviation weather impact through Saturday.
Spotty light showers may also develop Saturday morning through
midday (10% chance), but activity will mostly focus just north and
east of the terminals. E-SE winds will prevail through Saturday
morning with speeds mostly below 10 kts. Winds will then shift
W-SW at all terminals around 18-20Z Saturday and then back E in
the evening.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
West winds will prevail through most of the period at KIPL, while
winds at KBLH will vary between SSE and SW. Sustained speeds will
remain elevated, around 8-13 kts, through tonight at both
terminals. Minor LLWS may develop as surface winds subside
Saturday morning, but shear magnitudes are expected to stay below
TAF threshold. Lighter wind speeds (5-10 kts) and less gustiness 
is expected Saturday. SCT clouds down to 5K ft AGL are expected at
both terminals most of Saturday. Otherwise FEW to SCT mid and 
high clouds will continue to pass over the area.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Multiple weather systems are expected to move through the region
over the next week bringing multiple chances for showers and a few
storms to the area. One weather system is currently moving 
through central AZ this afternoon and a secondary one will move 
through tomorrow. Tomorrow's rain chances will be confined to the 
foothills and higher terrain areas north and east of Phoenix. In 
addition to the rain chances, these systems will cool temperatures
off below normal. Dry conditions and warmer temperatures are then
expected Sunday and Monday before another weather system moves 
through the region on Tuesday. A fourth weather system is then 
possible by the end of next week. These systems will bring 
additional rain chances to the region and cool temperatures back 
below normal. MinRHs will be around 30-60% through next week, with
excellent overnight recovery. Occasional wind gusts of 20-30 mph 
will continue through tomorrow afternoon, with the highest gusts 
associated with any shower activity and across the western 
districts. By tomorrow night, winds will return to their light and
diurnal patterns, with another period of gusty winds expected 
with the weather system on Tuesday.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least early next week due to 
water released from the dam. Water release levels have now risen to 
3000 cfs and are expected to remain at this release level through 
the next several days. This will have the potential to flood farm 
fields and low-water crossings along the river downstream from the 
dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Berislavich
LONG TERM...Ryan 
AVIATION...Benedict
FIRE WEATHER...Berislavich 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
